notes:
Account summary: Saffron Orbit is a large e-commerce personalization and support platform (1000+ employees). Primary goal is to move core personalization/ranking and customer chat inference to a Dedicated capacity with strict latency SLOs and predictable unit economics. They want a reserved capacity contract and strong SLAs (uptime + latency guarantees).

POC scope: Performance benchmarking on Redwood Dedicated. Focus areas: throughput guarantees, latency SLO validation, reserved GPU planning (A100 equiv sizing), and SLA negotiation points. Tests: load/ramp tests, concurrency/streaming tests, and 48h soak runs with representative production prompt mixes.

Representative workload details:
- Mix: 60% personalization/ranking (short prompts, reranking top-K), 30% chat-support (multi-turn, ~300 tokens average), 10% batch embeddings for nightly indexing.
- Token distribution: median request ~120 tokens; 95th percentile ~520 tokens (long support threads).
- Target SLOs (customer stated): p95 latency <= 150ms (inference-only), p99 <= 350ms for chat; throughput sustained 200 req/s baseline, burst to 500 req/s for seasonal spikes.
- Desired reserved capacity: initial ask = 8 GPU equivalents (A100-class) with autoscale headroom to +50% for peak.

POC test plan (executions & metrics):
1) Smoke & correctness: validate model responses for fidelity and fallback behavior (open-13B-int8 vs open-70B-q4).
2) Ramp/load test: linear ramp to 250 req/s over 30m, hold 2h, measure p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, memory, queue times.
3) Soak test: 48h at 150 req/s to detect degradation, mem growth, KV-cache hit-rate impacts.
4) Burst/resilience: simulated region failover and cold-cache stress; validate automatic fallback to smaller model variant under capacity pressure.
5) Cost/throughput profiling: token-level cost breakdown, batching efficiencies, effective tokens/sec/GPU.

Findings to date (high-level):
- Baseline (4 GPU equiv) handled short rerankers well; personalization latency p95 ~ 90ms.
- Chat p95 with open-70B-q4 at 150 req/s averaged ~170ms; tail p99 spiked to ~420ms during sustained ramps (KV-cache warmup identified).
- Soak run in progress: early signs show stable GPU mem usage but queueing increases when concurrency >200 without aggressive batching.
- Quantization (q4) reduces footprint and improves throughput but increases variability on p99 for long-context chat; team suggested caching and route-by-length policies.

Security/compliance notes:
- Required: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logging retention 3+ years, and data residency (us-east-1). SOC2 attestation delayed procurement.
- Legal requested explicit language for model output logging retention and pattern for redaction of PII.

Commercial/contract:
- Finance requests: 1) committed throughput pricing tiers (150, 300, 500 req/s), 2) unit-cost-per-1k-tokens at each tier, 3) SLA credits tied to p95 latency breaches and region failover RPO.
- Customer prefers annual reserved contract but wants a 3-month ramp clause to adjust reserved GPU count.

Customer quotes / call snippets:
- "Latency above 200ms on p95 for chat is a deal-breaker for our live support flows." (CTO, 2024-11-06).
- "We need guarantees that we won't face unbounded bill shocks during holiday spikes — committed throughput pricing is critical." (Head of Finance, 2024-12-05).

Open action items / next steps:
- Run final throughput test at 300 req/s with 8 GPU equiv and share detailed p95/p99 latency breakdown (owner: SE Miguel Torres) — target week of 2024-12-18.
- Provide SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration guide to Saffron security team (owner: Security + AE).
- Draft procurement term that includes 3-month ramp and explicit SLA credit mechanics for latency violations (owner: AE/legal).

POC blockers: SOC2 attestation pending (blocks procurement), legal data residency clauses still negotiating, need clearer definition of "inference-only" latency for SLA (does not include network egress).
